changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For heads of payments with international volume: 'Your approvals, market by market: where you have money left on the table, why it is happening, and what we will fix.' Lead with the customer's own approval rates by country, card type and issuer. Say 'approvals' instead of 'authorization rates', and do not lead with the average uplift.
changes.why: We pitched the average uplift, Stefan answered 'that's an average. What's mine?' and said 'I can't take an average to my CFO', and he talks in 'approvals' and 'Money left on the table', so the line needs to show his own numbers in his own words.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For accounts with international volume: 'A named payments-performance owner reviews your approvals with you every month, market by market.' Give the person's name, not a response-time tier.
changes.why: Stefan asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name, and he said 'I heard from Stripe when I said I was leaving', so his concern was ownership and proactive review, which response-time tiers do not answer.

changes.change: Renewal and competitive-defense offer for accounts with international volume, especially when the payments owner changes or a competitor proposes a traffic test: 'We will send you a market-by-market view of your own approvals, with the reasons and the fixes, within days.' Commit to the same timeline as any competitor test.
changes.why: Adyen won by testing on the customer's own traffic and reporting by country, and our market-by-market analysis, which Stefan called the most useful thing we'd sent him, arrived three weeks after he asked, when the test was already finished.
